findings.title: v2 accepts re-pinned semantic native-provider and implementation-role mismatches as Stable

Current candidate scopes model admission to current operator, policy, source, provider, model, effort, tools and environment, and rejects discovery-only, expired, failed-native and untrusted-configuration paths.
Current candidate preserves the admission revoke-CAS invariant: an in-flight successful verification cannot overwrite a concurrent revocation or newer verification.

limitations: Recovery2 continued the same fixed native reviewer session after the prior supervisor timed out without a report; no source, authority, credential, approval, Git, or native-conversation data was altered or read.

Independent byte audit verified the exact candidate SHA-256 078d6d48f83dfc0c52a107e0d5f7d2b23af46b76c649416629b3bd50641ad438, 182 manifest entries, and independently recomputed Git tree 20fdad924a966d4279ad347920f55588bb6c645a. All 178 evidence-manifest entries matched their recorded hashes; evidence-manifest.json is intentionally the sole unlisted self-manifest file.

Focused current dynamic evidence passed: Stable boundary suite 13 tests, release-provenance suite 14 tests, model-admission suite 30 tests, prior-session independent strict-v2 rejection checks, and recovery2's two semantic counterexamples. Recorded full-current regression evidence reports 574 Python tests; browser, host, frontend, syntax, baseline and rebuild records are byte-bound current evidence and were not needlessly rerun.

The decisive counterexamples re-pinned every enclosing v2 reference after changing the native receipt's provider/model-family semantics. A release-review labelled claude with a native receipt labelled codex and requested model gpt-6.1-sol still launched Stable; a purported implementation receipt labelled claude with a Claude model also still launched. The loader validates only release-review.provider and generic native-envelope fields, not receipt provider/model identity or the required Codex-implementation versus independent-Claude-review role binding.

The fix must bind and validate the actual native receipt provider against release-review.provider, bind implementation provenance to the required Codex role and reviewer provenance to the required independent Claude role for this task, and add rejection tests for re-pinned cross-provider/model/role evidence. A self-asserted release-review label is not an independent native identity proof.

Raw current metadata supports genuine Codex and Claude admission, sequential, concurrent fan-in, loop, lifecycle, exact-session recovery and no-double-writer workflows for this candidate. Provider-native transcripts and hidden reasoning were intentionally not supplied or read. Physical backend and effective effort remain unknown where the metadata records them as unknown.

The fixed external Gate, PR delivery/readback, authorized main merge, external hard approval, immutable installation, Stable launch/HTTP verification, unified-entry update and distinct user UX acceptance are post-review actions. They remain pending and are not treated as defects independent of the open source finding.
